hypotheses.expected_invariant: API health endpoint remains available and returns 200 during the fault window.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Killing the api container will expose the lack of replica redundancy and the absence of a load balancer, causing a full API outage until the restart policy recovers the container.
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: The restart=always policy should restart the container within a few seconds; after recovery, API health should return to 200 and the system should be clean.
hypotheses.validation_plan: Baseline: verify API health returns 200. Inject: kill the api container. Observe: monitor API health and HTTP response codes for 30 seconds. Oracle: check if health endpoint returns non-200 or connection refused during the kill window.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: The api service is a single instance with restart=always but no replicas; a pod kill will interrupt all HTTP requests and the healthcheck will fail until restart completes.

hypotheses.expected_invariant: API health and mock workflow response complete within the normal latency budget (e.g., <200ms).
hypotheses.hypothesis: Introducing 500ms latency on the redis service will expose the lack of timeouts or retry configuration in the api and worker services, causing request timeouts and degraded workflow execution.
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After removing the delay, latency should return to baseline and all services should recover without manual intervention.
hypotheses.validation_plan: Baseline: measure API response time and mock workflow latency. Inject: add 500ms latency to redis traffic. Observe: measure API response times and workflow completion for 30 seconds. Oracle: check if API response time exceeds expected threshold or workflow fails.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: Redis is a critical dependency for api, worker, worker_beat, and agent_backend; high latency will increase response times and may cause cascading timeouts.

hypotheses.expected_invariant: All API requests and workflow tasks succeed without retries or errors.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Causing 50% packet loss on the agent_backend service will expose the lack of retry logic in the api and worker services, leading to intermittent failures in agent-related operations.
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After removing the loss, all services should return to normal operation and no persistent errors should remain.
hypotheses.validation_plan: Baseline: run a set of API requests and workflow tasks to confirm success. Inject: apply 50% packet loss to agent_backend. Observe: monitor API success rate and workflow task completion for 30 seconds. Oracle: check if any requests fail or tasks are not completed.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: agent_backend is a critical dependency for api and worker; packet loss will cause connection resets and partial request failures.

hypotheses.expected_invariant: Database query latency remains within acceptable bounds and API health remains 200.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Stressing the MySQL container CPU to 80% will expose the lack of resource limits and connection pool tuning, causing slow queries and API timeouts.
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After stopping the CPU stress, MySQL should return to normal performance and all dependent services should recover.
hypotheses.validation_plan: Baseline: measure query latency and API response time. Inject: stress MySQL CPU to 80% for 30 seconds. Observe: monitor query latency and API health. Oracle: check if query latency exceeds threshold or API health degrades.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: db_mysql is a critical dependency for api, api_websocket, worker, worker_beat, and plugin_daemon; CPU saturation will degrade database performance and increase query latency.

hypotheses.expected_invariant: External HTTP requests to the frontend and API remain available.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Killing the nginx container will expose the lack of a load balancer and the single point of entry, causing a full frontend outage until the restart policy recovers it.
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: The restart=always policy should restart nginx quickly; after recovery, external access should be restored.
hypotheses.validation_plan: Baseline: verify external HTTP access to web and API. Inject: kill the nginx container. Observe: monitor HTTP access for 30 seconds. Oracle: check if external requests fail or return errors.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: nginx is the entry point for web and api traffic; a kill will interrupt all external access and the healthcheck will fail until restart.

hypotheses.expected_invariant: Workflow tasks complete within the expected time and no tasks are left unprocessed.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Adding 300ms latency to the worker service will expose the lack of retry or timeout configuration in the task queue, causing delayed task processing and potential task accumulation.
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After removing the delay, task processing should return to normal and any backlog should be cleared.
hypotheses.validation_plan: Baseline: submit a set of tasks and measure completion time. Inject: add 300ms latency to worker traffic. Observe: monitor task completion time and queue length for 30 seconds. Oracle: check if task completion time exceeds threshold or tasks remain pending.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: worker is a critical consumer of tasks and depends on agent_backend, db_mysql, db_postgres, redis, and seekdb; increased latency will slow task processing and may cause backlogs.

hypotheses.expected_invariant: All plugin executions succeed without errors.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Causing 30% packet loss on the plugin_daemon service will expose the lack of retry logic in agent_backend, leading to intermittent plugin execution failures.
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After removing the loss, plugin executions should return to normal and no persistent failures should remain.
hypotheses.validation_plan: Baseline: trigger a set of plugin executions and confirm success. Inject: apply 30% packet loss to plugin_daemon. Observe: monitor plugin execution success rate for 30 seconds. Oracle: check if any plugin executions fail.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: plugin_daemon is a critical dependency for agent_backend; packet loss will cause connection errors and plugin execution failures.

hypotheses.expected_invariant: Database query latency remains within acceptable bounds and API health remains 200.
hypotheses.hypothesis: Stressing the PostgreSQL container CPU to 60% will expose the lack of resource limits and connection pool tuning, causing slow queries and degraded API performance.
hypotheses.recovery_expectation: After stopping the CPU stress, PostgreSQL should return to normal performance and all dependent services should recover.
hypotheses.validation_plan: Baseline: measure query latency and API response time. Inject: stress PostgreSQL CPU to 60% for 30 seconds. Observe: monitor query latency and API health. Oracle: check if query latency exceeds threshold or API health degrades.
hypotheses.weakness_surface: db_postgres is a critical dependency for api, api_websocket, worker, worker_beat, and plugin_daemon; CPU saturation will degrade database performance and increase query latency.
